status_summary: No enacted law or bill found in this check caps the untaxed benefits employers may deduct. Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) moved the other way on two benefit-related preferences: section 70404 raised the tax-free dependent care assistance limit from 5,000 to 7,500 dollars for tax years beginning after 2025, and section 70401 raised the employer-provided child care credit to 40 percent (50 percent for eligible small businesses) with a 500,000 dollar annual cap (600,000 dollars for small businesses) for amounts paid after 2025. Neither is a cap on deductible benefits, and no rule on dependents aged 23 or older was found.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 section 70404 raised the section 129 dependent care assistance exclusion limit to 7,500 dollars (3,750 dollars for separate returns), effective for taxable years beginning after 2025 (per the amendment notes of 26 U.S.C. 129).

Public Law 119-21 section 70401 raised the section 45F employer-provided child care credit to 40 percent (50 percent for eligible small businesses) and the annual cap to 500,000 dollars (600,000 dollars for small businesses), effective for amounts paid or incurred after 2025 (per 26 U.S.C. 45F).

title: Cap untaxed employee benefits that employers deduct at 12,000 dollars per worker
uncertainties: No law or bill capping deductible employer benefits per employee was found. Public Law 119-21 raised the dependent care assistance limit (section 70404) and the employer child care credit (section 70401); both were confirmed on 2026-10-22 from the U.S. Code reproductions of 26 U.S.C. 129 and 45F hosted by law.cornell.edu, whose amendment notes cite the sections, dates and effective dates. An external retrieval of the enrolled text reports that no section of the law caps an employer deduction or an employee exclusion for benefits per worker; the govinfo.gov copy opened ends in Title I, so that whole-law absence finding is unverified, and other benefit changes in the law (for example the section 70204 exclusion for employer contributions to children's accounts) were not read. An external retrieval of Congress.gov and web searches (12 queries, run 2026-10-22; it cannot be reproduced here) found H.R. 8840 (Fair Care Act of 2026), introduced 2026-05-14 and referred to nine House committees with no later action, whose govinfo.gov status record carries no bill text; the retrieval reports that it caps the employee income exclusion for employer health coverage rather than the employer deduction the recommendation targets, so it is treated as related and does not change the stage. A health-exclusion bill reported in May 2026 could not be matched to a number, and H.R. 317 acts on the employee exclusion. The Treasury Unified Agenda rule list on reginfo.gov (headed 'Agency Rule List - 2026') lists benefit guidance, including a planned rule on Trump account contributions and dependent care programs, and no deduction cap. Checked systematically on 2026-10-19; Code pages and bill search refreshed 2026-10-22.
